Paul prays that their love would abound more and more. Who can you pray this for?
God who began a good work in you will bring it to completion. Where do you need this promise?
Paul's imprisonment advanced the gospel. How might God use your hard circumstances for good?
"To live is Christ, and to die is gain." What does this mean for you?
Paul urges them to live worthy of the gospel. What does that look like for you this week?
Paul says to count others more significant than yourselves. Where can you put others' interests first?
Christ humbled himself even to death on a cross, and God highly exalted him. What does his humility teach you?
God works in you, both to will and to work. How does this encourage you?
Do all things without grumbling, and shine as lights. What do you tend to grumble about?
Timothy and Epaphroditus genuinely cared for others. Who has cared for you like this?
Paul counted everything as loss compared to knowing Christ. What do you value most?
Paul wanted to know Christ and the power of his resurrection. How do you want to know Christ more?
Paul says he presses on toward the goal. What do you need to leave behind to press on?
Our citizenship is in heaven. How does this shape your priorities?
Paul urged two women to agree in the Lord. Is there a disagreement you could help heal?
Instead of being anxious, pray with thanksgiving, and God's peace will guard your heart. What anxiety can you pray about now?
Paul lists things to think about. What fills your mind most days?
Paul learned the secret of contentment through Christ who strengthens him. Where do you need contentment?
"My God will supply every need of yours." How has God provided for you?
